kata.name: probe composition seam: the billing/shipping joint check and the committed hand-merged baseline detect the same row — parity, with the eliminated merge step recorded as a gap
kata.series_verdict: pre-registered: detection arithmetic lands at parity — the hand-merged baseline carries the same seam equation, so the unique set is empty and the probe verdict is killed; the value claim under probe (eliminating the error-prone merge step) is a named gap, never a detection claim

expected.detail: floor control — a dangling `invoice_region` cell is already reported by the single-document check (exit 4); gluing the document with itself must show zero unique detections here (design Decision 5)

the billing/shipping seam: each document alone is clean, the joint run reports order `o3` invoiced north and dispatched south with the seam equation's declaring document attributed. The committed hand-merged baseline detects the same row, so the uniqueness axis derives parity (killed); the eliminated hand-merge step is recorded as a named gap, never a detection

commands: cargo run -q -p catherine-cli -- check crates/catherine-cli/tests/fixtures/gap_suite/composition_billing.ct.json crates/catherine-cli/tests/fixtures/gap_suite/composition_shipping.ct.json crates/catherine-cli/tests/fixtures/gap_suite/composition_seam_claim.ct.json --json  # exit 3, one violation/executed on row 2
cargo run -q -p catherine-cli -- check fixtures/probes/composition/hand_merged_seam.ct.json --json  # exit 3, the same witness

comparison.conventional_baseline: The conventional step is the manual hand-merge (Recipe D): the operator unions billing and shipping by hand and adds the seam equation, producing the committed fixtures/probes/composition/hand_merged_seam.ct.json. Executed with the same `check`, it reports the same violation/executed witness {equation: 0, row: 2, lhs: 0, rhs: 1} at order o3.

expressibility_gap.invariant: composition eliminates the manual hand-merge step (Recipe D)
expressibility_gap.why: the probe records detections only; the merge-step elimination is a workflow change outside the detection axis, so it is named here and never claimed as a unique detection

procedure: 1. The fault set and its expectations were committed in fixtures/probes/composition/faults.json and crates/catherine-ledger/src/catalog.rs before any run; nothing here is edited after the run.

2. The baseline arm executed the committed hand-merged document (fixtures/probes/composition/hand_merged_seam.ct.json, the hand union of the three gap-suite fixtures): exit 3 with one violation/executed witness {equation: 0, row: 2, lhs: 0, rhs: 1}.

3. The probe arm ran `check` over the three separate gap-suite documents: exit 3 with the same violation/executed witness, plus source attribution naming the seam-claim, billing, and shipping documents.
4. Elements were compared at fault level: both arms detect order o3 invoiced north and dispatched south, so unique_detections is empty.
5. The uniqueness axis derives killed for an empty unique set (parity). The merge-step elimination is recorded as a named expressibility gap on the entry — never as a detection claim.
